x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct: Andhra Pradesh has no coal of its own and draws coal from Singareni and MCL. Statement 3 is wrong: because its supply comes from these domestic sources (Singareni and MCL), its plants do not depend entirely on imported coal. So 1 and 2 only.

Small hydro plants up to 3 MW were transferred to MNRE in 1989, and the ceiling was raised to 25 MW in November 1999; today small hydro means up to 25 MW (MNRE) and large hydro above 25 MW (Ministry of Power). Options that reverse the two thresholds or dates are wrong.

All four are correct. Non-fossil sources are over 54% of capacity, yet coal, with only about 42% of capacity, gives over 70% of electricity; nuclear is about 1.6% of capacity but about 3% of generation (57 TWh in 2024-25). This is the capacity-generation paradox, so 1, 2, 3 and 4.

All three are correct. On 30 November 2025 thermal capacity was 246.90 GW, i.e. 48.45% of the 509.64 GW total; by August 2026 the total had risen to about 552 GW, with non-fossil sources above 54%. So 1, 2 and 3.
